plan:
**MAA – Coordinator Plan: Full‑Capability Audit for Project “Testing”** | Phase | Objective | Key Tasks | Responsible Specialist | Deliverable | |-------|-----------|-----------|------------------------|-------------| | **1. Scope & Definition** | Clarify what “everything you can do” means for the MAA system. | • Draft a capability inventory (language, reasoning, planning, data‑handling, safety, etc.)
• Define success metrics (accuracy, latency, robustness, compliance).
• Identify external interfaces (APIs, data feeds, user‑interfaces). | *Capability Analyst* | Capability Scope Document | | **2. Test Design** | Create a comprehensive test suite covering all identified capabilities. | • Map each capability to test cases (unit, integration, system, security, performance).
• Define input‑output expectations, edge‑cases, and failure modes.
• Establish automated test harnesses and manual test scripts. | *Test Engineer* | Test Plan & Test Cases | | **3. Environment Setup** | Prepare isolated, reproducible environments for testing. | • Provision compute resources (GPU/CPU clusters, containers).
• Configure data pipelines and mock data sources.
• Set up monitoring & logging infrastructure. | *DevOps Specialist* | Test Environment Blueprint | | **4. Execution & Data Collection** | Run tests, capture metrics, and log anomalies. | • Execute automated test runs (parallel where possible).
• Perform manual exploratory testing for edge scenarios.
• Log performance, errors, and security incidents. | *Test Engineer* + *Security Auditor* | Raw Test Results & Incident Log | | **5. Analysis & Validation** | Evaluate results against success metrics. | • Compute pass/fail rates, latency distributions, error rates.
• Conduct root‑cause analysis for failures.
• Verify compliance with safety & privacy guidelines. | *Data Analyst* + *Compliance Officer* | Analysis Report | | **6. Recommendations & Remediation** | Propose improvements and risk mitigations. | • Prioritize fixes (critical, high, medium, low).
• Suggest architectural changes or additional safeguards.
• Draft a remediation roadmap. | *Engineering Lead* + *Risk Manager* | Remediation Plan | | **7. Documentation & Knowledge Transfer** | Ensure audit findings are captured and shared. | • Update system documentation, capability matrix, and test artifacts.
• Conduct a knowledge‑sharing session with stakeholders.
• Archive audit artifacts in the MAA knowledge base. | *Documentation Specialist* | Final Audit Report & Knowledge Base Update | | **8. Continuous Improvement Loop** | Embed audit into ongoing operations. | • Schedule periodic re‑audits (quarterly).
• Integrate automated health checks into CI/CD.
• Monitor for drift or new risks. | *Operations Lead* | Continuous Improvement Plan | --- ### Timeline (Assuming 4‑Week Sprint) | Week | Activities | |------|------------| | 1 | Phase 1 & 2: Scope definition, test design, and documentation. | | 2 | Phase 3: Environment provisioning and test harness setup. | | 3 | Phase 4: Execute automated tests; begin manual exploratory testing. | | 4 | Phase 5–7: Analysis, remediation planning, documentation, and final audit report. | --- ### Success Criteria | Metric | Target | |--------|--------| | Test coverage | ≥ 95 % of identified capabilities | | Pass rate | ≥ 98 % of test cases | | Latency | ≤ 200 ms average for core inference | | Security compliance | Zero critical vulnerabilities | | Documentation completeness | 100 % of test cases documented | --- ### Final Deliverable A **Comprehensive Audit Report** containing: 1. Capability inventory & scope definition 2. Test plan & execution results 3. Analysis of performance, safety, and compliance 4. Remediation roadmap with priority levels 5. Updated documentation and knowledge‑base entries 6. Continuous improvement schedule This plan builds directly on the initial “test full capabilities” objective and provides a structured, specialist‑driven audit workflow to ensure every aspect of the MAA system is evaluated, documented, and improved.
